title: Second-Tier Stock Exchanges and Growth of Entrepreneurship
eligible_reason: Table 2 column (2) is a canonical staggered TWFE: reghdfe lnnstartup_c post0, absorb(countryind indyear) vce(cluster country) on a country-industry-year panel of VC-backed startups (Pitchbook). post0 is a 0/1 indicator equal to 1 in years after the country launched its first second-tier stock exchange (entryyear0 from the shipped Secondmktbycountry.dta; 51 non-US countries with launch years 1990-2019, 21 distinct launch years) and 0 otherwise; Pitchbook countries without a second-tier exchange are never treated; the US is excluded. Fixed effects are country-by-industry (unit) and industry-by-year (calendar time interacted with a time-invariant unit characteristic, allowed). No covariates, no weights, clustered by country. Published estimate (Log/T2_baseline_cyg.xml): 0.209 (0.069), N = 197,064. Column (1) has no fixed effects and column (3) adds four time-varying country controls (lngdp lnpop openess inflationGDP), so only column (2) qualifies in the main text. Caveats: (a) seven countries' exchanges closed (AE 1996-1999, BE 1996-2003, CH 1999-2002, DE 1996-2003, FR 1996-2000, IN 1990-2015, NZ 2007-2017), so post0 switches off; per PROTOCOL drop post-closure periods (the authors' Table IA7 instead drops these countries). (b) Early launchers (1990-1991: CA, DK, IN, PT, SG, JP, MY, PL, GB) may be always-treated depending on the panel start year, which is not verifiable without main_sample.dta. (c) The analysis file main_sample.dta sits in a 'Data for internal checking but not for public' folder that is NOT in the archive; only public inputs (treatment dates, World Bank controls, patents, trademarks) are shipped, so replication requires the authors' Pitchbook-derived panel. The Internet Appendix additionally reports a BJS imputation estimate (did_imputation lnnstartup_c countryind year entryyear0, autosample fe(countryind indyear); tau 0.349 (0.015), N 187,488, Table IA5 col 2), a stacked DiD (stackedev) and synthetic DiD (sdid), all on the same withheld file.
design_notes: Replicate Kit_0831: Readme_20260224.docx; Code/main_20250831_update.do (main-text Tables 1-7), Code/internetappendix_update.do (Tables IA1-IA9, Figure IA1), RawDataProcessing/*.sas and *.do (Pitchbook/USPTO cleaning, sample construction), Log/ (outreg2 xml/txt and smcl logs with published coefficients), Data to share/ (public inputs only). Sample construction (produce_sample_update2.do lines 49-52): main_sample = countryyrgrp_reg_20250314 (country x Pitchbook primary industry group x year counts of new VC-backed startups, nstartup_c, with lagged World Bank controls) keep if country~='US' & nmisctrl1==0 (GDP, population, openness, inflation non-missing) & inpb (country in Pitchbook). Treatment (main_pb_upload_update.do lines 263-267, 343-347): post0 = 1 if missing(exityear) & year>entryyear0, or year>entryyear0 & year<=exityear when the exchange closed; countries with several exchanges keep the earliest (lines 218-222 drop later launches for BE, FR, CH, AE, US). indyear = group(grp_num year); countryind = group(country grp_num). lnnstartup_c = ln(1 + nstartup_c) (IA4 analogue uses ln(v+1)). Outcome count panel built from a balanced 1990-2024 Pitchbook firm panel ('pitchbookfirm_balanced_9024'); exact year range of main_sample not visible in the package. Shipped treatment file Secondmktbycountry.dta: 52 countries (alpha2, entryyear0, entryyear1, exityear).

priority_note: Eligible design with a clean no-controls TWFE column (Table 2 col 2) and a BJS estimate in the appendix, but the regression sample is Pitchbook-derived and withheld; replication requires the authors to share main_sample.dta (or a Pitchbook licence to rebuild it with the shipped SAS/Stata code). Published coefficients are available in the Log folder for verification.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (SSRN working paper exists at 10.2139/ssrn.4470564 but was not consulted). Full-text flags: Borusyak, Goodman-Bacon, staggered, TWFE; cites Sun-Abraham, BJS, Roth et al., Cengiz et al. The abstract says 'additional tests for staggered difference-in-differences regressions', consistent with Table IA5 (stacked, BJS, sdid). Two items for the lead: (1) treatment switches off for seven closure countries (handle per Hull footnote 6 or follow IA7 and drop them); (2) BJS and other alternative estimators appear in the Internet Appendix rather than the main text as far as the package shows; re-check against the published article when text is available.
